Part 1 of **LIN-4395**: "A task shows the sessions that ran it, on one clock". This part adds no UI. It lands first, as its own PR.

**Where to read the parent.** Read LIN-4395's description: the `## As asked` block, `## Size of the move`, `## Design (chosen approach)` and `## Implementation Plan` (plan pass of 10 Nov at `b315e0e8f`). Then read the `### Plan Review Verdict` comment (Approve, comment `6ace09f6-de0d-45c1-a3e4-197be9aed902`) and its builder notes 1–4. **The parent's approved plan is where this piece starts.** Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4395.

**Why this piece exists.** Today a task's own reads stop at the 30-day reporting window, so a task older than a month shows no sessions. No dispatch has a working span either. This part fixes both where they live. Part 2 (the picture) reads what this part returns.

### Slice of the approved plan

**Files and approach**

* `lib/read-horizon.js`: name the rule and rewrite the header. Published reporting windows stay at 30 days: periodicals, `/kpis`, workspace spend, pipeline loops. A task's own reads (`/cost/:identifier` and the task page's timeline) cover its whole life. Drop `/cost` from the header's 30-day list. Export an explicit task-life bound. It **must be a** `Date`, because cross-type `$gte` fails (`read-horizon.js:36–40`). A missing `since` must still mean 30 days.
* New `lib/task-cost-read.js`: move the inline fetch out of the `/cost` route in `routes/proxy-compute.js`. The fetch is: own rows → founder identity → lineage siblings → `readCost({ perDispatch: true })`. Its substance does not change, and it is bounded by the task-life rule. The route becomes a caller. It keeps its validation, its 400s and its wire key order.
  * **Builder note 1, census:** `CALL_ALLOW.listInHorizon` (`tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js:68`) names `routes/proxy-compute.js`, not the new lib file. Keep the call-log `listInHorizon` read in the route and pass `appSummary` into `readTaskCost`. The timeline needs no app calls. The census then gets no new entry. If you move the read instead, replace the allowlist entry rather than adding one, and record why.
  * **Builder note 4:** pass the task-life bound as `since` to `listHistory` (optional there, because it is already bounded by identity key, `dispatch-store.js:310`) and to `listInHorizon`. Never pass it to `readCost` as `windowStart`: the guard at `cost-read.js:352–358` would drop lineages whose members have no `dispatchedAt`.
  * **Truncation (builder note 2):** `LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT` keeps the newest 2,000 rows. On a whole-life read, truncation therefore drops exactly the old rows this change newly admits. Keep the warning at `routes/proxy-compute.js:717`, and also *return* an incompleteness flag set from `lineageTotal > LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT`, so the picture can say "not complete".
* `/cost/:identifier` `window` becomes `{ days: null, appCallsSince: null, scope: 'task-life' }`. `scope` is the added key and goes last.
* `lib/cost-read.js` `dispatchesOf`: each entry gains ISO `firstRequestAt` / `lastRequestAt`. These are the min and max `at` of the request records that split rule C already assigns to that entry, or null when it owns none with a time. They are additive, and nothing else reassigns usage.
* `readCost` gains an opt-in `foundedElsewhere` result (plan Departure 2). It covers lineages founded on another issue that have a fetched member tagged with this issue (wake rows carry the child's `issueIdentifier`, `lib/dispatch-wake.js`). They are summarised by the same branches and carry `countedUnder` (the founder's identifier) plus the tagged itemIds. They are never added to `pricedUsd`/`totalUsd`. `groupLineageMembership` stays inside `cost-read.js` (`FOLD_IMPORTERS`). The opt-in adds no read, and `/cost` does not pass it.
* Correct the `lineageRecordsOverRecords` comment that says "every fetched member comes from a since-bounded read". The guard still applies when `windowStart` is passed.
* Consumers and docs: `lib/proxy-instructions.js` and `docs/proxy-integration.md` (window plus the two new fields; say that `totalUsd` for an old task is now whole-life). Update `scripts/survey-effort-analyse.mjs`: line 106 reads `cost.window?.appCallsSince` and line 135 prints "inside the 30-day app-call window" (builder note 3). Add `task-cost-read` to runs-and-dispatch in `docs/areas/areas.json`, and update `docs/architecture/source-map.md`.

**Testing strategy (witnesses: each fails before the change and passes after)**

* A lineage dispatched 40 days ago appears in `/cost/:identifier`. Rewrite the LIN-3161 suite in `tests/unit/proxy-issue-cost-route.test.js` to the new rule.
* Guard: the existing 30-day suites (periodicals, `/kpis`, pipeline loops) stay green unchanged. New assertion: `listInHorizon` with no `since` still bounds to 30 days.
* `firstRequestAt`/`lastRequestAt` follow split rule C: a late-posted record's `at` counts toward the dispatch it moves to, and a dispatch with no records reads null.
* Own figures are byte-identical with and without `foundedElsewhere`. A foreign lineage's cost is not in `pricedUsd`.
* Truncation: `lineageTotal > LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT` returns the incompleteness flag.
* Regenerate the cost-replay goldens (`scripts/cost-replay.mjs`). Explain every intentional change in `expected-changes.json`. **Builder note 2:** the list will be longer than "window + two fields". Corpus straddlers older than 30 days (`tests/fixtures/cost-replay/corpus.js` cases 4, 7, 16, 17) and over-cap fillers (cases 20–21) move S1's LIN-42/LIN-99 figures by design. Name each one and do not bend the code back to the old numbers.
* The census stays green with no new entry (or one swapped entry, per note 1).

**Acceptance**

* `/cost/:identifier` returns whole-life figures with `window.scope: 'task-life'`, and its validation, 400s and key order are unchanged.
* `readTaskCost` is callable from a non-route caller with no app-call summary, and returns the incompleteness flag.
* Per-dispatch `firstRequestAt`/`lastRequestAt` and the opt-in `foundedElsewhere` exist and are tested.
* Reporting windows are unchanged. Docs, instructions and the survey script are updated in the same PR.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4404 @ 3b1b57b15

**Short version:** the plan's code claims hold at `3b1b57b15`. The hard part is the frozen test baselines the plan doesn't name, plus a gap between the two aims: the old tasks this change admits are the ones with no working spans.

**Checked, holds**
- `listInHorizon` treats a missing `since` as 30 days (`llm-call-log.js:160`). `listHistory` treats it as no bound, because an identity key bounds the read (`dispatch-store.js:310–313`). The window guard drops members with no time (`cost-read.js:358`). The census pin is at `cost-read-census.test.js:68`, the warning at `proxy-compute.js:717`, and note 3's survey-script lines are 106 and 135.
- Foreign-founded lineages are already fetched. `anchors` (`proxy-compute.js:704`) is every lineage with a member row of this issue, not only the ones it founded (the comment above it says "founder of"). So `foundedElsewhere` needs no new read.

**Why it will be harder than it looks**
1. **Two more frozen baselines.** `goldens-lin4197.json` has the header `mustNotBeRegenerated`. Its `existingCorpusAtHead` and every stage's S1 carry `window.appCallsSince`. Two tests diff the live replay against it exactly: `cost-lin4197-replay.test.js:47–63` and `lin-4201-replay-change-list.test.js:39` and `:93`. The second asserts "the existing corpus … does not move at all". Whole-life S1 moves the corpus by design (note 2) and changes `window` in every section. The plan names only `goldens.json` and `expected-changes.json`. Expect to amend a "do not regenerate" baseline, with the reason in its header, and to check `lin4201-change-list.json` for new `dispatches[*].firstRequestAt` paths.
2. **A drift guard pins the old wording.** `lifetime-retention-contract-drift.test.js:163–166` requires `docs/passage-runner-prompt.md:182` to describe `/cost` as a "30-day app-call read window". That doc is a live agent prompt, and it isn't on the plan's docs list. Update both, deliberately. Also fix the stale comment at `dispatch-store.js:278` ("the 30-day fetch").
3. **Old tasks get lanes, not spans.** Request records started on 4 Nov (LIN-4202/4201). `dispatches`, and so `firstRequestAt`/`lastRequestAt`, exist only for `fold.source === 'records'` (`cost-read.js:521`). Every lineage older than 30 days is snapshot-only, with `dispatches: null`. The whole-life change and the spans don't overlap: Part 2's "working times unknown" outline will be the normal case for every task this part newly admits. That isn't a defect, but say it so nobody reads the empty spans as a bug.
4. **The incompleteness flag is coarse.** Per-lineage `incomplete` already catches truncation: the identity lookup is uncapped, so a truncated member is `missing` and `totalUsd` goes null. The route strips `incomplete` off the wire, though. The 2,000 cap is shared across all anchors, including a parent autopilot's whole lineage pulled in by one wake. So the flag can trip because of a lineage this task doesn't own. Return it, but let Part 2 also read per-lineage `incomplete`, which `readTaskCost` keeps.
5. **The bound's value matters.** An epoch `Date` passed to `listHistory` adds `dispatchedAt: {$gte}`, which skips rows with no `dispatchedAt` in Mongo. The replay fake (`harness.js:121`) filters them the same way, so neither path shows the difference. For `listHistory`, pass nothing (note 4 allows this). Use the explicit `Date` only for `listInHorizon`.

**What I'd do first:** widen only `since` in a throwaway change, then run `node scripts/cost-replay.mjs` and the two LIN-4197/4201 suites. That gives the full list of moving paths across all three baselines, and the list becomes the change-list items. Then lift `readTaskCost` with no change to behaviour, while the goldens hold.

## Survey global: LIN-4404 @ 3b1b57b15

**Where it lands.** The `/cost` route in `routes/proxy-compute.js` (1,682 lines of mostly unrelated routes), `lib/cost-read.js` and `lib/read-horizon.js`. The cost side has been improving fast. LIN-4147 → 4177 → 4178 → 4179 → 4201 → 4226 → 4263 → 4276 (2–5 Nov) merged several readers into one read, and `cost-read-census.test.js` keeps it that way. `/cost` is the last route that still builds a cost read's fetch inline. Moving that fetch out follows the direction the code is already going. The plan's line references still match this commit.

**What the obvious way would do**

- **Add a second whole-life rule.** A task-life read already exists. `horizon: 'all'` (`lib/pipeline-loops.js:880`, LIN-3328) means `since = null`, and the task page (`task-page-loader.js:1269`) and run evidence both use it. `read-horizon.js` doesn't mention it. A new exported task-life `Date` there would be a second name for the same rule. The `Date` is only *needed* for `listInHorizon` (`llm-call-log.js:160`, `since ?? readHorizonStart()`). `listHistory` by issue or `rootItemId` is already bounded by identity.
- **Promise spans that the target tasks won't have.** `dispatches` (and so `firstRequestAt`/`lastRequestAt`) is built only for records lineages (`usageDetailOf`, `cost-read.js:515`). Request records began around 4 Nov (LIN-4198/4201), and I found no backfill. A task older than 30 days, the case this piece exists for, will now come back whole-life but snapshot-only: `dispatches: null`, so no per-dispatch spans. Part 2 will have to fall back to lineage `dispatchedAt`/`durationMs`, or say the span isn't known. The ticket doesn't say this. It should be written down now so Part 2 doesn't find it the hard way.
- **Leave the new file unplaced, with nothing noticing.** In `docs/areas/areas.json`, runs-and-dispatch already names `task-cost`, which is dead: there is no `lib/task-cost.js`, it's left over from `buildTaskCost`. `task-cost-read` doesn't match that pattern, so the file would fall to the catch-all `^lib/`. No test would fail, because `area-map-placement.test.js` only checks the paths it lists.
- **Carry a wrong comment.** The route says "Every lineage this issue is the founder of" (`:702`). That's already wrong: anchors come from *any* member tagged with this issue, which is why `foundedElsewhere` needs no extra read. Fix the comment when moving it, don't copy it.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry**

- In `read-horizon.js`, name the task-life rule once and have `pipeline-loops`' `horizon: 'all'` point to it (header text, or one shared value). Don't add a parallel one.
- Replace the dead `task-cost` regex entry with `task-cost-read`, and add one `areaOf` assertion.
- In `proxy-integration.md`/`proxy-instructions.js`, say that `firstRequestAt`/`lastRequestAt` exist only where `dispatches` does. Add one witness: on a whole-life read, an old snapshot-only lineage returns `dispatches: null`.

**Better still, but not this task's**

- `proxy-compute.js` keeps collecting unrelated routes. Splitting it is a separate move.
- Giving pre-records lineages per-dispatch spans would need a records backfill from transcripts. That's a separate decision, and Part 2 should know it's missing rather than assume it exists.

## Implementation: LIN-4404

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2386 (branch `feat/lin-4404-task-life-cost-read`, commit `fa4bb76fb`). **CI:** green: `ci-success`, unit tests, E2E 1–4 and secret scan all pass.

**Delivered** (all of the acceptance list):
- `/cost/:identifier` returns whole-life figures with `window: { days: null, appCallsSince: null, scope: 'task-life' }`. Validation, 400s and wire key order are unchanged, and a test pins the key order.
- `readTaskCost` (`lib/task-cost-read.js`) can be called with no app-call summary. It returns `lineagesTruncated` (from `lineageTotal > LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT`) and keeps each lineage's `incomplete`.
- Each `dispatches` entry has `firstRequestAt`/`lastRequestAt`, following split rule C. `readCost` has the `foundedElsewhere` opt-in: own figures are byte-identical with it, and foreign cost stays out of `pricedUsd`. Both are tested.
- Reporting windows are unchanged: S2–S13 do not move in the replay, and `listInHorizon` with no `since` still bounds to 30 days. In the same PR: the docs, instructions, live passage-runner prompt, survey script and area map.
- Census: no new `CALL_ALLOW` entry. One redaction-census row moved with the three reads it counts. They had been keyed under `snapshots/diff`.

**Departures** are in the PR and on LIN-4395 (comment `4aee04df`): no `since` on `listHistory`; `TASK_LIFE_HORIZON` shared with pipeline-loops; `goldens.json` kept as the baseline, with change-list entry (g) added; `goldens-lin4197.json` amended with its reason; the cap flag kept off the wire.

**Witnesses:** each new test was run against the pre-change code and failed:
- Route suite: 7 failures.
- New cost-read suite: 11 of 15. The other four were checked by mutation.
- Agreement additions: 2.
- The `areaOf` assertion.

Local full unit suite: 24,724 of 24,725 pass. The one failure is the acorn CLI test, which fails the same way on an origin/main checkout here, so it comes from the local environment.

Merging is not this step's job.

### Leftovers

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2386. Head: `d84b2b1dba4b0d37d0b318c71b7662fe7efebf86`. CI green (`ci-success`, unit tests, E2E 1–4, secret scan).

- **Tidied:** `lib/cost-read.js`. `readCost` had a copy of `lineageRecords`' load step. Both now share `loadOnce`.
- **Tidied:** `LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT` moved from `routes/proxy.js` to `lib/task-cost-read.js`, its only consumer. Its comment there described the retired list-endpoint query and a 30-day window that no longer holds. `routes/proxy.js` re-exports it, and `readTaskCost` now uses it as the default cap, so Part 2 does not need to wire a cap.
- **Tidied:** comments the change made untrue:
  - the `createComputeRoutes` dep doc ("north-star endpoint");
  - `usageDetailOf`'s "the /cost route";
  - the route test's LIN-4147 and LIN-2615 notes (which also still named the retired `buildTaskCost`);
  - mongo-smoke's query note;
  - the source map.
- **Noted (lesson):** `docs/areas/agent-api.md` now records which frozen baselines a `/cost` window or shape change moves, and that `goldens.json` stays the baseline. It went there because `runs-and-dispatch.md` is at its 6,144-byte cap.
- **For close-out:** `tests/unit/lin-3384-redaction-census.test.js`. The scanner does not parse array route registrations (`router.get([...])`), so it keys those sites under the route registered above them. `/cost`'s three reads sat under `snapshots/diff` until this PR. Outside this change's area.
- **For close-out:** `scripts/survey-effort-analyse.mjs` keeps a fallback for a server from before this change (`appCallsSince`, 30 days). Delete it once #2386 is live.

No waiting entry was settled or made untrue by this change.

## Review — LIN-4404

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2386. Reviewed head `d84b2b1dba4b0d37d0b318c71b7662fe7efebf86`, based on `3b1b57b15`. It merges cleanly onto origin/main `f5b1f5efa`.

CI: green on `d84b2b1db`. Passing: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success. The Unit job runs `mongo-smoke` against a real `mongod`.

**Independent re-run (local, PR head):** I ran 11 suites, 200 of 200 pass: the new LIN-4404 suite, the route, cost-read, agreement, census, the LIN-4197 replay, the LIN-4201 change list, the retention drift guard, area placement, the redaction census and the cost callers.

### Scope check
The diff stays inside the plan's places plus the departures the survey named, recorded on LIN-4395 (`4aee04df`):
- `TASK_LIFE_HORIZON` is shared with pipeline-loops, so there is no second whole-life rule.
- `listHistory` gets no `since`.
- `goldens.json` stays as the baseline, with change-list entry (g).
